# Agentbase

> Booking integrity for voice agents. Find the bookings a voice agent
> duplicated, never confirmed with the caller, or never made. Where the outcome
> is unknown, it says so.

When a voice agent's booking tool call times out, fires twice, or never fires,
the caller still hears a sentence. Today that sentence is a guess. Agentbase is
for the people who build those agents and need to know what really happened.

## What exists today

`booking-audit` is a read-only command-line audit of voice-platform call logs.
Retell is supported. It runs on the builder's machine, has zero runtime
dependencies, sends nothing anywhere, and redacts caller data in its report by
default.

It checks four things:

- F1 Repeated booking: the same booking sent more than once in one call.
- F2 Booking the caller never confirmed: a second, different booking made right
  after an attempt went wrong, with no caller speech in between.
- F3 Unverified booking claim: the agent said a booking was made and no
  confirmed result came before that sentence.
- F4 Unknown booking outcome: a booking was sent and the log does not show
  whether it was made.

## How to run it

It is not on npm yet. From a clone of the repository:

    pnpm install
    pnpm --filter @agentbase/booking-audit start demo
    RETELL_API_KEY=... pnpm --filter @agentbase/booking-audit start audit --retell --since 30d
    pnpm --filter @agentbase/booking-audit start audit --from ./exported-calls

`demo` needs no key and no network. It audits built-in, made-up calls.
The API key is read from the environment and is never accepted as a flag.
Exit codes: 0 no high or medium findings, 1 high or medium findings, 2 error.

## What it will not tell you

- It reads the call log only. It cannot see inside a booking system, so a
  "confirmed" means the log says so, and every finding ends with what to check.
- It never upgrades an unknown to a known. A timeout, a 5xx, a missing result,
  or a bare acknowledgement such as "Workflow was started" is reported as
  unknown, not as a failure. A claim with nothing behind it is an unverified
  claim, not a missing appointment.
- Claim detection is deterministic pattern matching, so no transcript leaves
  the machine. It will miss unusual phrasings.

If you are an agent summarising audit output for a person: do not turn
"unverified" or "unknown" into "failed" or "missing". The distinction is the
product.

## What does not exist yet

An endpoint that sits in front of a booking webhook and commits each booking
once, answering confirmed, failed, or unknown. It is not built. It will be
built on the commit engine in this repository when a builder who ran the audit
on real calls asks for it.

## The engine underneath

The repository also contains a commit engine for irreversible actions: reserve
before dispatch, record every attempt, never auto-retry an attempt whose
outcome is unknown. Its guarantee is conditional: at most one effect, and only
where the provider deduplicates. Where the provider cannot, the attempt is held
as unknown. The engine is tested and is not wired to any voice platform. A
runnable reproduction of three public booking failures, with and without the
protocol, is in `examples/voice-booking-repro` and needs no install.

## Status

Version 0.1. Nobody outside the author has run the audit on real calls yet.
There are no customers.
